verses.zh: 以下所记的是摩西在约旦河东的旷野、疏弗对面的亚拉巴―就是巴兰、陀弗、拉班、哈洗录、底撒哈中间―向以色列众人所说的话。
verses.en: This is what[NOTE:1] Moses said to all of Israel in the Transjordanian[NOTE:2] wilderness, the arid rift valley opposite[NOTE:3] Suph,[NOTE:4] between[NOTE:5] Paran[NOTE:6] and Tophel,[NOTE:7] Laban,[NOTE:8] Hazeroth,[NOTE:9] and Di Zahab.[NOTE:10]
notes: Heb “These are the words.”

Heb “on the other side of the Jordan.” This would appear to favor authorship by someone living on the west side of the Jordan, that is, in Canaan, whereas the biblical tradition locates Moses on the east side (cf. v. 5). However the Hebrew phrase בְּעֵבֶר הַיַּרְדֵּן (beʿever hayyarden) is a frozen form meaning “Transjordan,” a name appropriate from any geographical vantage point. To this day, one standing east of the Jordan can describe himself as being in Transjordan.
The Hebrew term מוֹל (mol) may also mean “in front of” or “near” (cf. NCV, TEV, CEV, NLT).
This place is otherwise unattested and its location is unknown. Perhaps it is Khirbet Sufah, 4 mi (6 km) SSE of Madaba, Jordan.
The Hebrew term בֵּין (ben) may suggest “in the area of.”
Paran is the well-known desert area between Mount Sinai and Kadesh Barnea (cf. Num 10:12; 12:16).
Tophel refers possibly to eṭ-Ṭafîleh, 15 mi (25 km) SE of the Dead Sea, or to Dâbîlu, another name for Paran. See H. Cazelles, “Tophel (Deut. 1:1),” VT 9 (1959): 412-15.
Laban. Perhaps this refers to Libnah (Num 33:20).
Hazeroth. This probably refers to ʿAin Khadra. See Y. Aharoni, The Land of the Bible, 199-200.
Di Zahab. Perhaps this refers to Mina al-Dhahab on the eastern Sinai coast.

verses.zh: （从何烈山经过西珥山到加低斯・巴尼亚有十一天的路程。）
verses.en: Now it is ordinarily an eleven-day journey[NOTE:1] from Horeb[NOTE:2] to Kadesh Barnea[NOTE:3] by way of Mount Seir.[NOTE:4]
notes: An eleven-day journey was about 140 mi (233 km).
Horeb is another name for Sinai. “Horeb” occurs 9 times in the Book of Deuteronomy and “Sinai” only once (33:2). “Sinai” occurs 13 times in the Book of Exodus and “Horeb” only 3 times.

Kadesh Barnea. Possibly this refers to ʿAin Qudeis, about 50 mi (80 km) southwest of Beer Sheba, but more likely to ʿAin Qudeirat, 5 mi (8 km) NW of ʿAin Qudeis. See R. Cohen, “Did I Excavate Kadesh Barnea?” BAR 7 (1981): 20-33.
Mount Seir is synonymous with Edom. “By way of Mount Seir” refers to the route from Horeb that ended up in Edom Cf. CEV “by way of the Mount Seir Road”; TEV “by way of the hill country of Edom.”

verses.zh: 出埃及第四十年十一月初一日，摩西照耶和华藉着他所吩咐以色列人的话都晓谕他们。
verses.en: However, it was not until[NOTE:1] the first day of the eleventh month[NOTE:2] of the fortieth year[NOTE:3] that Moses addressed the Israelites just as[NOTE:4] the Lord had instructed him to do.
notes: Heb “in” or “on.” Here there is a contrast between the ordinary time of eleven days (v. 2) and the actual time of forty years, so “not until” brings out that vast disparity.
The eleventh month is Shebat in the Hebrew calendar, January/February in the modern (Gregorian) calendar.
The fortieth year would be 1406 b.c. according to the “early” date of the exodus. See E. H. Merrill, Kingdom of Priests, 66-75.
Heb “according to all which.”

verses.zh: 那时，他已经击杀了住希实本的亚摩利王西宏和住以得来、亚斯他录的巴珊王噩。
verses.en: This took place after the defeat[NOTE:1] of King Sihon[NOTE:2] of the Amorites, whose capital was[NOTE:3] in Heshbon,[NOTE:4] and King Og of Bashan, whose capital was[NOTE:5] in Ashtaroth,[NOTE:6] specifically in Edrei.[NOTE:7]
notes: Heb “when he struck [or “smote”].”
See Deut 2:26-3:22.
Heb “who lived.”
Heshbon is probably modern Tell Hesban, about 7.5 mi (12 km) south southwest of Amman, Jordan.
Heb “who lived.”
Ashtaroth is probably Tell ʿAshtarah, about 22 mi (35 km) due east of the Sea of Galilee.
Edrei is probably modern Derʿa, 60 mi (95 km) south of Damascus (see Num 21:33; Josh 12:4; 13:12, 31).

verses.zh: 摩西在约旦河东的摩押地讲律法说：
verses.en: So it was in the Transjordan, in Moab, that Moses began to deliver these words:[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “this instruction”; KJV, NIV, NRSV “this law”; TEV “God’s laws and teachings.” The Hebrew noun תּוֹרָה (torah) is derived from the verb יָרָה (yarah, “to teach”) and here it refers to the Book of Deuteronomy, not the Pentateuch as a whole.

verses.zh: 「耶和华―我们的　神在何烈山晓谕我们说：你们在这山上住的日子够了；
verses.en: The Lord our God spoke to us at Horeb and said, “You have stayed[NOTE:1] in the area of this mountain long enough.
notes: Heb “lived”; “dwelled.”

verses.zh: 要起行转到亚摩利人的山地和靠近这山地的各处，就是亚拉巴、山地、高原、南地，沿海一带迦南人的地，并黎巴嫩山又到幼发拉底大河。
verses.en: Head out[NOTE:1] and resume your journey. Enter the Amorite hill country, and all its neighboring areas, including the rift valley,[NOTE:2] the hill country, the foothills,[NOTE:3] the Negev,[NOTE:4] and the coastal plain—all of Canaan and Lebanon as far as the Great River, that is, the Euphrates.
notes: Heb “turn”; NAB “Leave here”; NIV, TEV “Break camp.”

As a geographic feature the rift valley (עֲרָבָה, ʿaravah) extends from Galilee to the Gulf of Aqaba. The reference here probably includes the Jordan Valley and continues to the wider part of the rift valley below the Dead Sea. Some versions transliterate the name as Arabah (ASV, NAB, NIV, NRSV).

The שְׁפֵלָה (shephelah) is the geographical region between the Mediterranean coastal plain and the hill country, sometimes called the “western foothills” (NIV, CEV, NLT), “Judean foothills” (HCSB), “lowland” (NASB, ESV), or by the Hebrew “Shephelah” (NRSV).

The Negev is the area of central, southern Judah, south of the hill country and Beer Sheba and west of the rift valley. As a geographic feature it is a depression extending south to the gulf of Aqaba, but the reference here is probably to the northern portion of the region.

verses.zh: 如今我将这地摆在你们面前；你们要进去得这地，就是耶和华向你们列祖亚伯拉罕、以撒、雅各起誓应许赐给他们和他们后裔为业之地。」
verses.en: Look! I have already given the land to you.[NOTE:1] Go, occupy the territory that I,[NOTE:2] the Lord, promised[NOTE:3] to give to your ancestors[NOTE:4] Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and to their descendants.”[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “I have placed before you the land.”
Heb “the Lord.” Since the Lord is speaking, it is preferable for clarity to supply the first person pronoun in the translation.
Heb “swore” (so NAB, NIV, NRSV, NLT). This refers to God’s promise, made by solemn oath, to give the patriarchs the land.
Heb “fathers” (also in vv. 11, 21, 35).
Heb “their seed after them.”

verses.zh: 「那时，我对你们说：『管理你们的重任，我独自担当不起。
verses.en: I also said to you at that time, “I am no longer able to sustain you by myself.

verses.zh: 耶和华―你们的　神使你们多起来。看哪，你们今日像天上的星那样多。
verses.en: The Lord your God has increased your population[NOTE:1] to the point that you are now as numerous as the very stars of the sky.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “multiplied you.”
Or “heavens.” The Hebrew term שָׁמַיִם (shamayim) may be translated “heaven(s)” or “sky” depending on the context.

verses.zh: 惟愿耶和华―你们列祖的　神使你们比如今更多千倍，照他所应许你们的话赐福与你们。
verses.en: Indeed, may the Lord, the God of your ancestors, make you a thousand times more numerous than you are now, blessing you[NOTE:1] just as he said he would!
notes: Heb “may he bless you.”

verses.zh: 但你们的麻烦，和管理你们的重任，并你们的争讼，我独自一人怎能担当得起呢？
verses.en: But how can I alone bear up under the burden of your hardship and strife?

verses.zh: 你们要按着各支派选举有智慧、有见识、为众人所认识的，我立他们为你们的首领。』
verses.en: Select wise and practical[NOTE:1] men, those known among your tribes, whom I may appoint as your leaders.”
notes: The Hebrew verb נְבֹנִים (nevonim, from בִּין [bin]) is a Niphal referring to skill or intelligence (see T. Fretheim, NIDOTTE 1:652-53).

verses.zh: 你们回答我说：『照你所说的行了为妙。』
verses.en: You replied to me that what I had said to you was good.

verses.zh: 我便将你们各支派的首领，有智慧、为众人所认识的，照你们的支派，立他们为官长、千夫长、百夫长、五十夫长、十夫长，管理你们。
verses.en: So I chose[NOTE:1] as your tribal leaders wise and well-known men, placing them over you as administrators of groups of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens, and also as other tribal officials.
notes: Or “selected”; Heb “took.”

verses.zh: 「当时，我嘱咐你们的审判官说：『你们听讼，无论是弟兄彼此争讼，是与同居的外人争讼，都要按公义判断。
verses.en: I furthermore admonished your judges at that time that they[NOTE:1] should pay attention to issues among your fellow citizens[NOTE:2] and judge fairly,[NOTE:3] whether between one person and a native Israelite[NOTE:4] or a resident foreigner.[NOTE:5]
notes: Or “you.” A number of English versions treat the remainder of this verse and v. 17 as direct discourse rather than indirect discourse (cf. KJV, NAB, NIV, NRSV, NLT).
Heb “brothers.” The term “brothers” could, in English, be understood to refer to siblings, so “fellow citizens” has been used in the translation.

The Hebrew word צֶדֶק (tsedeq, “fairly”) carries the basic idea of conformity to a norm of expected behavior or character, one established by God himself. Fair judgment adheres strictly to that norm or standard (see D. Reimer, NIDOTTE 3:750).

Heb “between a man and his brother.” The first use of “brother” in this verse refers broadly to fellow citizens. This second use is narrower, being in opposition to the “resident foreigner.” The גֵּר (ger) “resident foreigner” was not simply a foreigner (Hebrew נֵכָר; nekar) but was essentially a naturalized citizen and had equal protection under the law. This is one of the verses designed to ensure that equal treatment (see also Deut 10:16-19; 16:18-20; Exod 12:49; Num 15:16, 29).
On the Hebrew ger (גֵּר) “resident foreigner,” see notes at Exod 12:19 and Deut 29:11.

verses.zh: 审判的时候，不可看人的外貌；听讼不可分贵贱，不可惧怕人，因为审判是属乎　神的。若有难断的案件，可以呈到我这里，我就判断。』
verses.en: They[NOTE:1] must not discriminate in judgment, but hear the lowly[NOTE:2] and the great alike. Nor should they be intimidated by human beings, for judgment belongs to God. If the matter being adjudicated is too difficult for them, they should bring it before me for a hearing.
notes: Heb “you,” and throughout the verse (cf. NASB, NRSV).
Heb “the small,” but referring to social status, not physical stature.

verses.zh: 那时，我将你们所当行的事都吩咐你们了。」
verses.en: So I instructed you at that time regarding everything you should do.

verses.zh: 「我们照着耶和华―我们　神所吩咐的从何烈山起行，经过你们所看见那大而可怕的旷野，往亚摩利人的山地去，到了加低斯・巴尼亚。
verses.en: Then we left Horeb and passed through all that immense, forbidding wilderness that you saw on the way to the Amorite hill country as the Lord our God had commanded us to do, finally arriving at Kadesh Barnea.

verses.zh: 我对你们说：『你们已经到了耶和华―我们　神所赐给我们的亚摩利人之山地。
verses.en: Then I said to you, “You have come to the Amorite hill country, which the Lord our God is about to give[NOTE:1] us.
notes: The Hebrew participle has an imminent future sense here, although many English versions treat it as a present tense (“is giving us,” NAB, NIV, NRSV) or a predictive future (“will give us,” NCV).

verses.zh: 看哪，耶和华―你的　神已将那地摆在你面前，你要照耶和华―你列祖的　神所说的上去得那地为业；不要惧怕，也不要惊惶。』
verses.en: Look, he[NOTE:1] has placed the land in front of you![NOTE:2] Go up, take possession of it, just as the Lord, the God of your ancestors, said to do. Do not be afraid or discouraged!”
notes: Heb “the Lord your God.” The pronoun (“he”) has been used in the translation for stylistic reasons, to avoid repetition.
Or “has given you the land” (cf. NAB, NIV, NRSV).

verses.zh: 你们都就近我来说：『我们要先打发人去，为我们窥探那地，将我们上去该走何道，必进何城，都回报我们。』
verses.en: So all of you approached me and said, “Let’s send some men ahead of us to scout out the land and bring us back word as to how we should attack it and what the cities are like there.”

verses.zh: 这话我以为美，就从你们中间选了十二个人，每支派一人。
verses.en: I thought this was a good idea,[NOTE:1] so I sent[NOTE:2] twelve men from among you, one from each tribe.
notes: Heb “the thing was good in my eyes.”
Or “selected” (so NIV, NRSV, TEV); Heb “took.”

verses.zh: 于是他们起身上山地去，到以实各谷，窥探那地。
verses.en: They left and went up to the hill country, coming to the Eshcol Valley,[NOTE:1] which they scouted out.
notes: Or “the Wadi Eshcol” (so NAB).sn The Eshcol Valley is a verdant valley near Hebron, still famous for its viticulture (cf. Num 13:22-23). The Hebrew name “Eshcol” means “trestle,” that is, the frame on which grape vines grow.

verses.zh: 他们手里拿着那地的果子下来，到我们那里，回报说：『耶和华―我们的　神所赐给我们的是美地。』
verses.en: Then they took[NOTE:1] some of the produce of the land and carried it back down to us. They also brought a report to us, saying, “The land that the Lord our God is about to give us is good.”
notes: The Hebrew text includes “in their hand,” which is unnecessary and somewhat redundant in English style.

verses.zh: 「你们却不肯上去，竟违背了耶和华―你们　神的命令，
verses.en: You were not willing to go up, however, but instead rebelled against the Lord your God.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “the mouth of the Lord your God.” To include “the mouth” would make for odd English style. The mouth stands by metonymy for the Lord’s command, which in turn represents the Lord himself.

verses.zh: 在帐棚内发怨言说：『耶和华因为恨我们，所以将我们从埃及地领出来，要交在亚摩利人手中，除灭我们。
verses.en: You complained among yourselves privately[NOTE:1] and said, “Because the Lord hates us he brought us from Egypt to deliver us over to the Amorites so they could destroy us!
notes: Heb “in your tents,” that is, privately.

verses.zh: 我们上哪里去呢？我们的弟兄使我们的心消化，说那地的民比我们又大又高，城邑又广大又坚固，高得顶天，并且我们在那里看见亚衲族的人。』
verses.en: What is going to happen to us? Our brothers have drained away our courage[NOTE:1] by describing people who are more numerous[NOTE:2] and taller than we are, and great cities whose defenses appear to be as high as heaven[NOTE:3] itself! Moreover, they said they saw[NOTE:4] Anakites[NOTE:5] there.”
notes: Heb “have caused our hearts to melt.”
Heb “greater.” Many English versions understand this to refer to physical size or strength rather than numbers (cf. “stronger,” NAB, NIV, NRSV; “bigger,” NASB).
Or “as the sky.” The Hebrew term שָׁמַיִם (shamayim) may be translated “heaven(s)” or “sky” depending on the context.
Heb “we have seen.”

Heb “the sons of the Anakim.”sn Anakites were giant people (Num 13:33; Deut 2:10, 21; 9:2) descended from a certain Anak whose own forefather Arba founded the city of Kiriath Arba, i.e., Hebron (Josh 21:11).

verses.zh: 我就对你们说：『不要惊恐，也不要怕他们。
verses.en: So I responded to you, “Do not be terrified[NOTE:1] of them!
notes: Heb “do not tremble and do not be afraid.” Two synonymous commands are combined for emphasis.

verses.zh: 在你们前面行的耶和华―你们的　神必为你们争战，正如他在埃及和旷野，在你们眼前所行的一样。
verses.en: The Lord your God is about to go[NOTE:1] ahead of you; he will fight for you, just as you saw him do in Egypt[NOTE:2]
notes: The Hebrew participle indicates imminent future action here, though some English versions treat it as a predictive future (“will go ahead of you,” NCV; cf. also TEV, CEV).
Heb “according to all which he did for you in Egypt before your eyes.”

verses.zh: 你们在旷野所行的路上，也曾见耶和华―你们的　神抚养你们，如同人抚养儿子一般，直等你们来到这地方。』
verses.en: and in the wilderness, where you saw him[NOTE:1] carrying you along like a man carries his son. This he did everywhere you went until you came to this very place.”
notes: Heb “the Lord your God.” The pronoun (“him”) has been employed in the translation for stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 你们在这事上却不信耶和华―你们的　神。
verses.en: However, through all this you did not have confidence in the Lord your God,

verses.zh: 他在路上，在你们前面行，为你们找安营的地方；夜间在火柱里，日间在云柱里，指示你们所当行的路。」
verses.en: who would go before you on the way to find places for you to camp, appearing in a fire at night and in a cloud by day to show you the way you ought to go.

verses.zh: 「耶和华听见你们这话，就发怒，起誓说：
verses.en: When the Lord heard you, he became angry and made this vow:[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and swore,” i.e., made an oath or vow.

verses.zh: 『这恶世代的人，连一个也不得见我起誓应许赐给你们列祖的美地；
verses.en: “Not a single person[NOTE:1] of this evil generation will see the good land that I promised to give to your ancestors!
notes: Heb “Not a man among these men.”

verses.zh: 惟有耶孚尼的儿子迦勒必得看见，并且我要将他所踏过的地赐给他和他的子孙，因为他专心跟从我。』
verses.en: The exception is Caleb son of Jephunneh;[NOTE:1] he will see it and I will give him and his descendants the territory on which he has walked, because he has wholeheartedly followed me.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Caleb had, with Joshua, brought back to Israel a minority report from Canaan urging a conquest of the land, for he was confident of the Lord’s power (Num 13:6, 8, 16, 30; 14:30, 38).
Heb “the Lord.” The pronoun (“me”) has been employed in the translation, since it sounds strange to an English reader for the Lord to speak about himself in third person.

verses.zh: 耶和华为你们的缘故也向我发怒，说：『你必不得进入那地。
verses.en: As for me, the Lord was also angry with me on your account. He said, “You also will not be able to go there.

verses.zh: 伺候你、嫩的儿子约书亚，他必得进入那地；你要勉励他，因为他要使以色列人承受那地为业。
verses.en: However, Joshua son of Nun, your assistant,[NOTE:1] will go. Encourage him, because he will enable Israel to inherit the land.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the one who stands before you”; NAB “your aide”; TEV “your helper.”
Heb “it”; the referent (the land) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 并且你们的妇人孩子，就是你们所说、必被掳掠的，和今日不知善恶的儿女，必进入那地。我要将那地赐给他们，他们必得为业。
verses.en: Also, your infants, who you thought would die on the way,[NOTE:1] and your children, who as yet do not know good from bad,[NOTE:2] will go there; I will give them the land and they will possess it.
notes: Heb “would be a prey.”

Do not know good from bad. This is a figure of speech called a merism (suggesting a whole by referring to its extreme opposites). Other examples are the tree of “the knowledge of good and evil” (Gen 2:9), the boy who knows enough “to reject the wrong and choose the right” (Isa 7:16; 8:4), and those who “cannot tell their right hand from their left” (Jonah 4:11). A young child is characterized by lack of knowledge.

verses.zh: 至于你们，要转回，从红海的路往旷野去。』
verses.en: But as for you,[NOTE:1] turn back and head for the wilderness by the way to the Red Sea.”[NOTE:2]
notes: The Hebrew pronoun is plural, as are the following verbs, indicating that Moses and the people are addressed (note v. 41).

Heb “the Reed Sea.” “Reed” is a better translation of the Hebrew סוּף (suf), traditionally rendered “red.” The name “Red Sea” is based on the LXX which referred to it as ἐρυθρᾶς θαλάσσης (eruthras thalassēs, “red sea”). Nevertheless, because the body of water in question is known in modern times as the Red Sea, this term was used in the translation. The part of the Red Sea in view here is not the one crossed in the exodus but its eastern arm, now known as the Gulf of Eilat or Gulf of Aqaba.

verses.zh: 「那时，你们回答我说：『我们得罪了耶和华，情愿照耶和华―我们　神一切所吩咐的上去争战。』于是你们各人带着兵器，争先上山地去了。
verses.en: Then you responded to me and admitted, “We have sinned against the Lord. We will now go up and fight as the Lord our God has told us to do.” So you each put on your battle gear and prepared to go up to the hill country.

verses.zh: 耶和华吩咐我说：『你对他们说：不要上去，也不要争战；因我不在你们中间，恐怕你们被仇敌杀败了。』
verses.en: But the Lord told me: “Tell them this: ‘Do not go up and fight, because I will not be with you and you will be defeated by your enemies.’”

verses.zh: 我就告诉了你们，你们却不听从，竟违背耶和华的命令，擅自上山地去了。
verses.en: I spoke to you, but you did not listen. Instead you rebelled against the Lord[NOTE:1] and recklessly went up to the hill country.
notes: Heb “the mouth of the Lord.” See note at 1:26.

verses.zh: 住那山地的亚摩利人就出来攻击你们，追赶你们，如蜂拥一般，在西珥杀退你们，直到何珥玛。
verses.en: The Amorite inhabitants of that area[NOTE:1] confronted[NOTE:2] you and chased you like a swarm of bees, striking you down from Seir as far as Hormah.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “in that hill country,” repeating the end of v. 43.
Heb “came out to meet.”
Hormah is probably Khirbet el-Meshash, 5.5 mi (9 km) west of Arad and 7.5 mi (12 km) SE of Beer Sheba. Its name is a derivative of the verb חָרָם (kharam, “to ban; to exterminate”). See Num 21:3.

verses.zh: 你们便回来，在耶和华面前哭号；耶和华却不听你们的声音，也不向你们侧耳。
verses.en: Then you came back and wept before the Lord, but he[NOTE:1] paid no attention to you whatsoever.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the Lord.” The pronoun (“he”) has been employed in the translation here for stylistic reasons, to avoid redundancy.
Heb “did not hear your voice and did not turn an ear to you.”

verses.zh: 于是你们在加低斯住了许多日子。」
verses.en: Therefore, you remained at Kadesh for a long time—indeed, for the full time.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “like the days which you lived.” This refers to the rest of the forty-year period in the desert before Israel arrived in Moab.
